tagline: An old turnpike over the ridges, with a canal for company.
intro: Route 57 runs northeast out of Greenwich Township on the line of an 1806 turnpike between Phillipsburg and Morristown, and a Lenape trail before that. It keeps to the farmland of the Pohatcong Creek valley between Pohatcong and Scotts mountains, passes through Washington, and in its eastern miles comes within sight of the Musconetcong River on the way to Hackettstown.
The Morris Canal shared the corridor, carrying Pennsylvania anthracite across New Jersey until the state abandoned it in 1924. Pieces of it still turn up beside the road.

moments.title: New Village
moments.text: A marker names a mile of Route 57 here as New Jersey's first concrete highway, laid in 1912 with cement from Edison's works in town, the company that later supplied Yankee Stadium.

moments.title: Port Murray
moments.text: Named for a president of the canal company, Port Murray keeps a canal boat basin, and from here the canal ran 11 miles on a single level to Saxton Falls.

moments.title: Hackettstown
moments.text: At the end of the route a mile of canal channel and towpath survives in Florence Kuipers Memorial Park, with a guard lock at Saxton Falls in Stephens State Park.
